q: detailed explanation of the french revolution
write a detailed explanation of the french revolution
a: The French Revolution (1789-1799) was a period of radical social and political change in France that began with the storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789 and ended with Napoleon Bonaparte's coup in 1799. Its causes included: massive state debt from wars (especially the American Revolution), regressive taxation that burdened the Third Estate (commoners) while exempting the clergy and nobility, crop failures and bread shortages in 1788-89 leading to famine, Enlightenment ideas spreading concepts of popular sovereignty and rights, and resentment of the absolutist monarchy of Louis XVI. Key events: the Tennis Court Oath (June 1789), the Storming of the Bastille (July 14, 1789), the abolition of feudalism (August 1789), the Declaration of the Rights of Man (August 1789), the Women's March on Versailles (October 1789), the Civil Constitution of the Clergy (1790), the Flight to Varennes (June 1791), the Reign of Terror (1793-1794) led by the Committee of Public Safety, and the Thermidorian Reaction (July 1794). The Revolution had enormous consequences: it ended absolute monarchy in France, established the principle of popular sovereignty, spread nationalist and republican ideals across Europe, led to the Napoleonic Wars, influenced revolutions in Haiti and Latin America, and established the framework for modern French society including the metric system, civil code, and secular education.
